data.narrative:
Oishii, a Series C robotics and manufacturing company founded by Hiroki Koga and Brendan Somerville, has raised $386M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of nine private robotics firms at Series B–D stages, supplemented by one public comparable.

Two triangulation methods apply directly. Stage-progression analysis applies a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical for Series C advancement, yielding $656M based on total capital raised as a proxy. Peer-median methodology anchors to seven same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables—including Exotec ($2.0B, Series D), Dexterity ($1.6B, Series B), Hadrian ($1.6B, Series D), and Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B, Series B)—producing a median valuation of $1.6B with a range of $1.0B–$2.0B.

These methods triangulate to a range of $557M (low) to $1.9B (high), with a median of $1.2B. The 70% spread between stage-progression and peer-median reflects ambiguity around Oishii's relative market position within the peer cohort and the applicability of earlier-stage comp valuations to a later-stage round. Key uncertainties include capital efficiency relative to peers, revenue scale and growth trajectory, and whether peer valuations reflect near-term market corrections in the robotics sector. The $1.2B median represents the central estimate absent additional proprietary performance data.
